expectation: ICOS is a membrane marker on a subset of activated or follicular-helper-like T cells. I would expect rare to moderate, discrete membrane-ringed cells inside CD3+ T cell areas, clustered in lymphoid aggregates and scattered singly in stroma, with no signal in CD3-negative tissue.
observed: A: many discrete cell-sized yellow spots across most tissues, denser in aggregate-like zones. Two tiles show diffuse haze that follows the tissue. B and C: sparse, with only a few cells. D: a bright cell with a clear membrane ring. E: ICOS clusters sit within CD3-dense tissue, and some cells are white (ICOS and CD3).
why: Discrete, cell-sized, membrane-ringed ICOS+ cells are scattered and clustered in CD3-rich zones across many tissues, as expected for activated T cells.
notes: A distinct sparse population of membrane-ringed cells, clustered where CD3+ T cells are dense and partly co-expressing CD3. Two tiles carry diffuse haze, but it doesn't change the verdict.
